basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1-2.' and it opens 'VERS. 1, 2.-- Venerunt duo angeli Sodomam vespere, sedente Lot in foribus civitatis, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1, 2.-- Venerunt duo angeli Sodomam vespere, sedente Lot in foribus civitatis, et caetera. Quare Abraham in tribus viris, si Deum intellexit, vel angelos, et iterum Lot in duobus eos humano cibo vesci putabat? Fortasse prius esse homines arbitrati sunt; in quibus Deum loqui intellexerunt, quibusdam divinae majestatis existentibus et apparentibus | signis, postea fuisse angelos cognoverunt, cum eis videntibus in coelum issent.
